successStories.title: How Nexora helped a growing technology company build its engineering leadership team
successStories.challenge: A Series B technology company needed to hire a VP of Engineering and four engineering managers within six months to support rapid product expansion. Previous attempts with other agencies had produced mismatched candidates and slow timelines.
successStories.strategy: We ran a retained executive search with dedicated market mapping across 40 target companies, combining behavioural interviewing with technical assessment panels and culture-fit sessions led by the founder.
successStories.result: All five leadership roles filled within five months, with a 100% retention rate at the 18-month mark. The new leadership team scaled engineering headcount from 30 to 90 within a year.
successStories.imageAlt: Team of professionals in a modern office meeting

successStories.title: Scaling a clinical workforce for a telehealth provider expanding into 12 new states
successStories.challenge: A telehealth company expanding into 12 new states needed to hire 80 licensed clinicians and 20 care coordinators within four months while maintaining strict licensing and compliance requirements.
successStories.strategy: We deployed a dedicated RPO team, built state-specific candidate pipelines, managed licensing verification, and ran coordinated interview days to accelerate decision-making.
successStories.result: 102 hires completed in 14 weeks, with full licensing compliance. Time-to-fill reduced by 40% compared to their internal recruitment, and a 95% offer-acceptance rate.

successStories.title: Building a finance transformation team for a private equity portfolio company

blog.title: How to negotiate your salary without burning bridges
blog.excerpt: Salary negotiation is one of the most important — and most uncomfortable — conversations in a job search. Here is a framework for doing it with confidence and professionalism.
blog.imageAlt: Two professionals discussing work with a laptop
blog.content: Salary negotiation is a skill, not a gamble. The key is preparation: know your market value, understand the full compensation package, and frame the conversation around mutual value rather than personal need. Start by researching comparable roles using salary surveys and market data. When the offer arrives, express enthusiasm first, then ask thoughtful questions about the package. Anchor on data, not emotion. And remember — the best negotiations leave both sides feeling respected and excited to work together.

blog.title: The STAR method: structure your answers for behavioural interviews
blog.excerpt: Behavioural interviews ask you to describe past situations. The STAR method gives you a clear structure to answer concisely and powerfully every time.
blog.imageAlt: Successful job interview handshake in an office
blog.content: The STAR method — Situation, Task, Action, Result — is the most reliable framework for answering behavioural interview questions. Start by briefly setting the scene (Situation), explain what you were responsible for (Task), describe what you specifically did (Action), and finish with the measurable outcome (Result). Prepare 5-7 versatile stories in advance, practice them aloud, and always quantify your results. The goal is to show, not tell, how you think and work.

blog.title: 5 signs your hiring process is costing you great candidates
blog.excerpt: Top talent doesn't stay on the market long. If your process has any of these five warning signs, you may be losing your best candidates before you even make an offer.
blog.imageAlt: Colleagues discussing documents in a corporate meeting
blog.content: The best candidates are off the market in 10 days. If your hiring process takes longer, you are losing. Five red flags: overly long interview rounds, lack of communication between stages, no flexibility on interview scheduling, vague job descriptions, and slow feedback after interviews. Fix these and you will see higher offer-acceptance rates and a stronger employer brand.

blog.title: The rise of the hybrid workforce: what it means for hiring in 2025
blog.excerpt: Hybrid work is no longer a perk — it is an expectation. Here is how leading companies are structuring hybrid policies and what it means for your hiring strategy.
blog.imageAlt: Open office with colorful dividers and cityscape view
blog.content: Hybrid work has become the default for knowledge workers. The companies winning the talent war are those offering flexibility with intentionality — clear in-office days for collaboration, remote days for deep work, and investment in digital collaboration tools. Hiring strategies must now compete on flexibility, not just compensation.

blog.title: What makes a great CTO? Lessons from 50 executive searches
blog.excerpt: After 50 CTO searches, we have noticed patterns in what separates the good from the great. It is rarely about technology — it is about people and judgment.
blog.imageAlt: Professionals discussing charts during a business meeting
blog.content: Great CTOs are not the strongest individual technologists — they are leaders who can translate business strategy into technical vision, build and retain world-class teams, and make sound judgment calls under uncertainty. In our executive searches, the candidates who succeed are those who demonstrate commercial acumen, people leadership and a learning mindset, not just technical depth.

blog.title: Why employer branding is your cheapest source of great talent
blog.excerpt: Companies with strong employer brands see 50% lower cost-per-hire and 28% lower turnover. Here is how to build one without a massive budget.
blog.imageAlt: Diverse group of professionals in a boardroom meeting
blog.content: Employer branding is not a marketing exercise — it is a talent strategy. Start by asking your current employees what they love about working there, then tell those stories authentically across your careers site, social channels and candidate communications. Authenticity outperforms polish. Companies with strong employer brands reduce cost-per-hire by up to 50% and improve retention by 28%.
